title: Mary J
content: This is what I saw five days prior to my mother's death, then again two days prior, and again before my mother died. My mom was a very difficult person to be around. She was affectionately known as "Mean Jean" by my sister and me. She was a cruel alcoholic who made my life extremely hard for me. I was terrified of her and completely controlled by her. I honestly don’t recall much kindness from her. I distanced myself from her for two years before she died. In 2007, my dad got sick and passed away on November 15. Mom had been in the hospital with pneumonia and was released for Dad’s funeral. I was afraid to see her because I was in trouble for not visiting her during those two years. She was readmitted to the hospital immediately after the funeral and placed in the ICU, because she was near death herself. I did visit her while she was hospitalized. After a month in a coma, she woke up and began improving. My siblings lived far away, so I knew I would be the sole caregiver. This was a deeply unsettling thought, but I accepted it as my fate. I visited her on December 30, 2007, in room 529. I sat at the end of her bed and talked with her. She was scheduled for physical therapy the following week and would then be released. I truly believed she would do whatever it took to recover enough to go home. On December 31, 2007, I was trying to stay awake until midnight but dozed off; although it didn’t feel like sleeping. I saw my mother in room 529, her head tipped all the way back, with a tube filled with water but the tube wasn’t attached to anything. I watched the water run out of the tube. Somehow, I knew I could call the nurse or let the water run out. I let it run out. The moment the tube was empty, I saw an incredibly bright light under my eyelids. This was like when you close your eyes in sunlight. I wasn’t in the light but looking at it. At the center was an even brighter circle. I knew, without doubt, that God was taking her to heaven. I don’t know how I knew, but I did. I woke up immediately and rushed to check if the hospital had called. They hadn’t called. I waited until morning to call my sister and tell her about this strange dream. Three nights later, I was lying on the couch in my family room while my kids watched TV. This time, I was wide awake but had my eyes closed. The light with the brighter circle appeared again. There were no lights on in the room, just the TV. Two days later, on January 5, 2008, I was getting ready for work at 4:30 AM. The hospital called and told me to come. When I arrived, I entered her room. She was still in room 529. I saw her head tipped back with a tube in her throat. The tube had been disconnected from the breathing machine. I later learned her head was tilted back because they had tried to intubate her. She had passed away. I’ve always wondered why I chose not to save her in the dream and have felt a bit selfish for letting her go. But I believe God was reassuring me she was with him in heaven because I would have always feared the alternative. I’m not psychic. Nothing like this has happened before or since. But I saw my mother’s death and what I believe was heaven’s light. Sometimes, when I wonder if near-death experiences are just the dying brain’s activity, I think of this. My brain wasn’t shutting down, and I saw what I saw. It hasn’t happened since.

elements.At the time of your experience, was ther: No, I was under immense anxiety due to my mother’s illness., Other (briefly specify), I didn’t die, but I saw a death and the incredibly bright light.
elements.How did your highest level of consciousn: More consciousness and alertness than normal, I was extremely alert and certain that what I saw was real. After seeing the bright light the first time, I opened my eyes gasping and shaking. It was so real that I almost called my sister at midnight. But, I worried she would think I was losing my mind.
elements.At what time during the experience were: I was most conscious and alert on Thursday night when I saw the light for the second time.
elements.Did you see, or feel surrounded by, a br: A light clearly of mystical or other-worldly origin
elements.Did you see an unearthly light?: Yes, I’ve never have seen anything brighter. The awareness of what this light is was certain.
elements.What emotions did you feel during the ex: I felt guilty for not trying to save her.
elements.Did scenes from the future come to you?: Scenes from my personal future, Just my mom’s death.
elements.What was your religion prior to your exp: Christian- Catholic, I was raised strictly Catholic. I feared that if you were a bad person, you would not be allowed into Heaven. I was deeply afraid that my mother might not be a good candidate for Heaven because she was cruel and a troublemaker. Nevertheless, she was my mom.
elements.What is your religion now?: Other or several faiths, I am mostly spiritual now. I struggle with the rules of organized religion because I no longer believe that God is spiteful, waiting to catch us sinning, even though that is how I was raised.
elements.Did your experience include features con: Content that was both consistent and not consistent with the beliefs you had at the time of your experience, I was taught that Heaven exists but not everyone gets to go. Who knows, maybe that is still true. Maybe the Catholic Church is telling the truth. I had a priest administer Last Rites, so perhaps that helped. I have no idea.
elements.Did you have a change in your values and: Uncertain, I now have a clearer sense of what I believe is to come, rather than hoping I'm 'good enough' to get there.
elements.Did you encounter or become aware of any: Uncertain, I’ve wondered if the circle of even brighter light was Jesus. At the time, that was my thought. I have no idea if it is the case.
elements.During your experience, did you gain inf: Yes, The light is all I have to go on, but it sure felt universal and so comforting to me. I wonder if this experience actually wasn’t for her, but for me.
Yes, I know that bright light was showing me she was going to be with God.
elements.Did you gain information about how to li: Yes, Yeah, I’m thinking we all must go to Heaven, not just the people who don’t hurt others.
elements.What life changes occurred in your life: It saddens me that I can no longer fully believe what the Catholic Church taught me. I loved much about the church growing up, despite the guilt and demands. I still feel a sense of belonging in a church, but I disagree with many teachings. I remain spiritual in a more open way, exploring Buddhist teachings and other religious mystics. Seeing that light was significant because my brain wasn't shutting down, so it couldn't have been a hallucination. I wasn't seeking spiritual answers those nights; if anything, I felt abandoned by God.
elements.How accurately do you remember the exper: I remember the experience more accurately than other life events that occurred around the time of the experience, I have not forgotten a single detail about either of the two times I saw the bright light or the day of her passing. The memories remain vivid and unchanged. I no longer feel as guilty about letting the water run out as I once did.
elements.Do you have any psychic, non-ordinary or: Uncertain, I've had moments where I felt a strange knowing about deceased loved ones, as if they wanted me to convey messages to those left behind. Once, I told a grieving stranger that his mother wasn't angry and thanked him for caring for her. It didn't feel made up. At another funeral, I sensed a hand on my shoulder, though it wasn't physically there.
elements.Are there one or several parts of your e: Despite her challenges, I'm glad she is in Heaven. I would have worried all these years otherwise.
elements.What did you believe about the reality o: Experience was definitely real, The bright light was real. The first time I saw the light could be dismissed as a dream. But the second time it happened, with its inexplicable brightness, defies other explanations. I was fully awake.
elements.What do you believe about the reality of: Experience was definitely real, It remains unchanged; exactly what I saw then.
elements.Is there anything else that you would li: I wonder if others have had similar experiences, like Mark Twain possibly did.
elements.Did the questions asked and information: Yes, It didn't involve much, and I remember it exactly as it happened.
